findings.issue_text: [BUG] getCalendarCredentials still calls getCalendar(credential) synchronously, so item.calendar is now a Promise<Calendar | null> rather than a Calendar. getConnectedCalendars was patched to `await item.calendar`, but any other consumer of getCalendarCredentials that touches item.calendar directly (destructured usages of { calendar }) gets a Promise object; truthiness checks like `if (!calendar)` always pass and calls like calendar.deleteEvent are missing from the Promise, throwing TypeError at runtime wherever getConnectedCalendars is not the only caller.

[BUG] Converting the forEach callback to async makes rejections escape the surrounding try/catch that previously caught synchronous throw, and the returned promises are discarded by forEach. A failing calendar deleteEvent during a Vital reschedule now surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection instead of hitting the catch block; the deletion is silently skipped with no logged error, leaving orphaned external calendar events after a reschedule.

[BUG] Converting the forEach callback to async makes rejections escape the surrounding try/catch and discards the returned promises. A failing calendar deleteEvent during a wipemycalother reschedule becomes an unhandled promise rejection, silently skipping event deletion instead of being caught and logged, leaving orphaned external calendar events.

[BUG] Converting the forEach callback to async discards the returned deleteEvent promises, so the surrounding code that previously collected/awaited these operations (via the callback return path) no longer observes completion. Calendar event deletion on reschedule is fire-and-forget: the tRPC mutation can return success before the external calendar event is actually deleted, and any rejection is an unhandled promise rejection with no error surfaced to the user or logs, causing orphaned external events.

[BUG] The inner `forEach(async (credential) => { ... })` converts the callback to async while the loop over updatedBookings awaits getCalendar inside it, discarding all resulting deleteEvent promises. Recurring-booking deletion inside handleCancelBooking pushes nothing back to the outer await Promise.all of apiDeletes (the async forEach returns immediately), so the HTTP response returns before external calendar events for recurring bookings are deleted and any rejection is unhandled, leaving orphaned external events.

[ADVISORY] getCalendarCredentials still calls getCalendar() synchronously, so the `calendar` field it builds is now a raw Promise while getConnectedCalendars is patched to `await item.calendar`, leaving the field's consumers split between two conventions. Any consumer of getCalendarCredentials outside this diff that reads `item.calendar` directly (e.g. checks calendar.credentialId or calls calendar methods) now receives a Promise where the declared type Calendar | null promises a value; the next developer copying from getConnectedCalendars' non-await twin sites ships a silent break where calendars appear truthy and never resolve.

[BUG] `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.forEach(async (credential) => {...})` converts the callback to async without awaiting it, so recurringEvent update/delete work runs detached from the request handler. When the dynamic import behind getCalendar rejects (module load failure), the rejection surfaces as an unhandledRejection that can crash the Node process instead of a caught error, and the handler responds success before calendar updates complete — previously the synchronous getCalendar could not throw.

[BUG] `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` fires async callbacks that the surrounding code never awaits, and the `return calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` return value is silently discarded by forEach. Reschedule completes and the booking is updated while calendar/video deletions are still in flight; a rejection from the awaited getCalendar dynamic import becomes an unhandledRejection with no stack tie to the request, whereas the pre-diff code's deleteEvent promises were at least launched synchronously before any await could interleave.

[BUG] Identical detached `forEach(async ...)` pattern: async callbacks are never awaited and their returned deleteEvent/deleteMeeting promises are discarded. Same failure mode as the vital twin: reschedule proceeds before remote deletions settle, and dynamic-import rejections inside the async callback become unhandled promise rejections.

[BUG] `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` makes the reschedule handler's per-reference cleanup async-but-unawaited, discarding the returned deleteEvent promise. The tRPC reschedule mutation returns before calendar events are deleted; a dynamic-import failure inside getCalendar yields an unhandledRejection rather than a trpc error the client could see.

[ADVISORY] The entire appStore is converted from resolved modules to pending dynamic-import Promises in a sweeping cross-package refactor, yet the diff contains no test files (no *.test.*, *.spec.*, spec/, test/ paths) verifying any of the awaited call-site conversions. A single missed await at any appStore consumer outside the diff compiles away nothing at runtime — the site silently receives a Promise (truthy, fails the `"lib" in app` check with a TypeError on a Promise lacking `lib`) and the integration is reported 'not implemented' with no test to catch the regression; the async-conversion behaviors (getVideoAdapters rewrite, deleteEvent async, getConnectedCalendars await) are all unverified.

[ADVISORY] The getVideoAdapters rewrite from reduce to for-loop is behavior-bearing new logic (it fixes the old early-`return acc` that skipped subsequent credentials) with no test in the diff. If the rewrite regresses (e.g. awaiting appStore mis-handles an app name without a store entry), users with multiple video credentials lose availability merging in getBusyVideoTimes, double-booking across video providers, with no spec to catch it.

[ADVISORY] The module still eagerly loads every app package at evaluation time, so the PR's stated intent of deferring package loading is not actually achieved. Anyone expecting startup/import-time savings or true lazy loading gets none: `import("./applecalendar")` etc. are invoked immediately when app-store/index.ts is evaluated, kicking off all chunk fetches at once — only the await points became async, not the loading. In a server bundle this is roughly equivalent to the old static imports; the diff converts the whole codebase to async call sites without delivering the corresponding benefit.

[BUG] Converting the recurring-event cancellation loop's forEach callback to async defers the apiDeletes pushes until after the surrounding code has already collected and awaited them, so recurring-event deletions are dropped from the awaited batch. For a recurring booking cancellation, the loop awaits getCalendar before pushing the delete/update promises; any caller that does Promise.all(apiDeletes) immediately after the forEach resolves without those deletions, and failures inside the async callbacks surface as unhandled rejections. Previously getCalendar was synchronous so the pushes happened before collection — this diff introduces the race.

[ADVISORY] getCalendarCredentials still assigns `const calendar = getCalendar(credential)` without awaiting, silently changing the field type from Calendar|null to Promise<Calendar|null> while leaving the function's signature and any out-of-diff consumers unaware. The invariant "calendar is a Calendar or null" is no longer enforced by types at this boundary; the one in-diff consumer is patched (line 47 `await item.calendar`), but any other caller of getCalendarCredentials outside this diff now holds a Promise and will silently produce `if (!calendar)`-style checks that always pass, breaking null-guarding logic elsewhere.

[ADVISORY] The migration preserves the broken `forEach(async ...)` fire-and-forget pattern: the awaited getCalendar/deleteEvent work inside the callback is never awaited by anyone, so this site's migration is incomplete relative to the PR's own goal. Reschedule-time calendar deletions for vital (and the identical copy in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts and packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx around line 553) run detached from the surrounding try/catch and response flow — errors become unhandled rejections and the reschedule response can return before deletions complete, with no way for the caller to observe failure.

[BUG] getCalendarCredentials calls the now-async getCalendar without await, so the `calendar` it puts into each result object is a Promise<Calendar|null> rather than a Calendar. getConnectedCalendars was patched (line 47: `await item.calendar`) but the objects returned by getCalendarCredentials now carry a Promise in the `calendar` slot; any other consumer of getCalendarCredentials that reads `.calendar` (and TypeScript itself, since the inferred type no longer matches Calendar | null) gets a truthy Promise where it expects a Calendar — `if (!calendar)` checks pass for null wrapped in a Promise, and calendar.method calls hit Promise.prototype, producing runtime type errors in every calendar-resolution path not updated in this diff.

[BUG] The forEach callback was made async, so its returned deleteEvent promise is discarded and never awaited by the surrounding try block. Errors from calendar.deleteEvent now surface as unhandled promise rejections instead of being caught by the enclosing try/catch, and Reschedule returns before the external calendar events are actually deleted — a failed delete leaves orphaned events on the remote calendar with no retry and no log, silently breaking reschedule cleanup for vital bookings.

[BUG] The forEach callback was made async, so its returned deleteEvent promise is discarded and never awaited by the surrounding try block. Errors from calendar.deleteEvent now surface as unhandled promise rejections outside the try/catch, and Reschedule returns before remote calendar events are deleted — failed deletes leave orphaned events with no error handling, silently breaking reschedule cleanup for wipemycal bookings.

[BUG] bookingRefsFiltered.forEach was converted to an async callback whose returned deleteEvent promise is discarded, so the reschedule handler does not await external deletions and does not observe their failures. The tRPC reschedule mutation resolves and the booking is marked rescheduled before remote calendar events are actually deleted; a failed deleteEvent becomes an unhandled rejection and the old event persists on the user's calendar alongside the newly created one — a double-booking on the external calendar.

[BUG] The forEach callback over user credentials was made async, so the awaited getCalendar and the subsequent updateEvent calls run detached from the request handler's control flow. For recurring-event cancellation, the handler returns a response (and the transaction/request completes) while remote calendar updates for subsequent occurrences are still in flight; failures in those updates are unhandled rejections and recurring bookings are left out of sync across the user's calendars with no error surfaced to the user.

[ADVISORY] The dynamic import() calls are invoked eagerly at module-evaluation time inside the appStore object literal, so every app package still loads at startup — the diff adds async ceremony without achieving lazy loading. The stated goal (async import of appStore packages, reduced startup bundle/work) is not achieved: all 28 packages are still imported at process start, now additionally as 28 floating promises; whoever later 'optimizes' by assuming modules load on first use will be wrong, and startup gets no benefit from this refactor while every call site pays an await.

[ADVISORY] The 28 unhandled import() promises created at module load have no .catch, so a single failed dynamic import (e.g. a broken optional peer dependency in one app package) becomes a process-wide unhandledRejection. In any deployment where one app package fails to load (native dep missing, syntax error introduced), the whole server process dies on unhandledRejection (or logs it at boot) even for tenants that never use that app — a single app's failure cascades to all tenants, the exact failure mode the appStore isolation was meant to prevent.

[ADVISORY] getVideoAdapters awaits each appStore dynamic import sequentially inside a for-of loop, serializing module resolution for N credentials. Availability checks (getBusyVideoTimes) over many video credentials now pay N sequential await round-trips instead of the previous synchronous construction; with several integrations this adds avoidable latency on the booking availability path. Since the imports were already kicked off at module load, awaiting in parallel (Promise.all) is strictly better and costs nothing.

[BUG] getCalendarCredentials still calls getCalendar() synchronously, so the `calendar` field it puts into each credential entry is now a Promise, not a Calendar instance. Every consumer of the exported getCalendarCredentials other than getConnectedCalendars (which happens to `await item.calendar`) receives a truthy Promise where it expects a Calendar or null — truthiness checks like `if (!calendar)` never fire for unimplemented calendar types, and calling e.g. `calendar.deleteEvent(...)` on a Promise throws TypeError, breaking cancellation/inspection flows that relied on the null contract.

[BUG] Changing forEach's callback to async silently detaches the awaited deletion work from the surrounding control flow, so Reschedule's try/catch no longer captures errors and the function can proceed/return before deleteEvent completes. A failing calendar deleteEvent during reschedule now produces an unhandled promise rejection instead of being caught by the try block, and a rescheduling response can be sent before the old event is deleted on the external calendar — the original intent (observe deletion outcome during reschedule) is silently lost.

[BUG] The async forEach callback discards the awaited deleteEvent promises, removing them from the try/catch and from the function's completion. Errors from calendar deletion during wipemycalother reschedule become unhandled rejections instead of caught errors, and deletion runs detached from the reschedule flow — same silent behavior change as the vital copy, and the duplicated hand-edited blocks have already drifted in lockstep, which is the exact hazard of the copy-paste.

[BUG] bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) discards the awaited deleteEvent promise, so the router's surrounding try/catch and any code that assumed deletion completed before continuing no longer observes it. The `return calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` inside the async forEach callback returns to nowhere; a rejection during reschedule deletion surfaces as an unhandled rejection after the response, so failures that previously surfaced as handled errors now vanish from the request lifecycle.

[BUG] The dynamic import() calls are evaluated eagerly at module-init of packages/app-store, so every one of the 28 app packages starts loading the moment any file imports appStore — the PR's stated objective of deferring appStore package loading is not achieved. Any serverless function or client bundle importing appStore transitively still kicks off all 28 package fetches at import time; cold-start and bundle-size savings the change was accepted for never materialize, while the whole codebase pays the async access cost — an objective change nobody accepted the tradeoff for. To get real laziness the store needs `() => import(...)` thunks or top-level await decisions per app.

[ADVISORY] getVideoAdapters now awaits each appStore entry sequentially in a for-of loop instead of the previous parallel reduce, serializing 28 dynamic-import resolutions per call. Every createMeeting/deleteMeeting/getBusyVideoTimes call waits for imports one-by-one; once modules are cached this is negligible, but the first request after cold start pays serialized round-trips across all of a user's video credentials — the conversion from reduce to for-of was not required by the async change (a Promise.all over the map preserves the original parallel intent).

[BUG] `await appStore[paymentAppCredential?.app?.dirName as keyof typeof appStore]` awaits a possibly-undefined store entry, and the subsequent `console.warn` interpolates the awaited value which is `undefined` when the dirName is unknown — but more importantly the `as keyof typeof appStore` cast now hides that every value in appStore is a Promise, so any out-of-diff consumer of appStore that was not migrated (the diff only updates a handful of sites) reads a Promise where it expects a module. appStore's public shape changed from `Record<string, App>` to `Record<string, Promise<App>>` with no deprecation or type-level migration aid; every call site outside this diff (webhook handlers, app-store UI pages, oAuth flows) still does `appStore[name].lib` and now gets `undefined` on `.lib`, silently breaking app loading across the repo — the diff shows no audit that all consumers were updated.

[BUG] Changing the forEach callback to async makes every calendar deleteEvent a fire-and-forget Promise that the surrounding code never awaits. The old booking's calendar events are deleted in the background while the reschedule flow continues; a rejected deleteEvent becomes an unhandled rejection and the try/catch around the loop never catches it, so on failure the old calendar event silently remains (orphaned event on the user's calendar) with no retry or error surfaced.

[BUG] The async forEach callback's returned deleteEvent Promise is discarded because forEach ignores callback return values. Identical to the vital copy: cancellation-time calendar deletions run unawaited; a slow or failed dynamic import plus deleteEvent means the reschedule completes while the old external calendar event may still exist, and any error is lost as an unhandled rejection outside the try block.

[BUG] bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) discards the awaited deleteEvent Promise, so the loop is not awaited by the tRPC handler. The reschedule mutation returns before the old booking's calendar events are actually deleted; if the process exits or the dynamic import rejects, the external calendar event is orphaned with no error propagated to the user, and the surrounding try/catch can never observe the failure.

[BUG] The recurring-event deletion path uses forEach(async ...) whose Promises are never awaited or collected into apiDeletes' awaited Promise.all. For recurring-booking cancellation, calendar event deletions race the request lifecycle; a failed await getCalendar/deleteEvent is swallowed as an unhandled rejection and the user's calendar keeps events for a booking that Cal.com reports as cancelled — silent data divergence between the app and the external calendar.

[ADVISORY] getCalendarCredentials now stores an unawaited Promise<Calendar|null> in each item's calendar field while only one consumer (getConnectedCalendars line ~47) was updated to `await item.calendar`. Any other current or near-future consumer of getCalendarCredentials that reads item.calendar directly gets a Promise instead of a Calendar, and `'calendar' in item` style checks pass while `calendar.deleteEvent` would throw TypeError on the Promise; the next change to this file gets riskier because the invariant (sync value vs Promise) depends on the consumer's discipline.

[BUG] forEach(async ...) discards the returned deleteEvent/deleteMeeting promises, so rejections are unhandled and the enclosing try/catch cannot catch them. During reschedule, a failing calendar deleteEvent rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection while the reschedule itself completes and reports success, leaving the stale calendar event on the remote provider with no log, no error result, and no rollback.

[BUG] forEach(async ...) discards the returned deleteEvent/deleteMeeting promises, so rejections are unhandled and the enclosing try/catch cannot catch them. During reschedule, a failing calendar deleteEvent rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection while the reschedule completes and reports success, orphaning the old event on the remote calendar with no surfaced error.

[BUG] forEach(async ...) discards the returned deleteEvent promises, so rejections are unhandled by any surrounding error handling. A reschedule whose calendar deleteEvent rejects still returns a successful tRPC response; the old event stays on the user's calendar and the rejection surfaces only as an unhandled promise rejection, invisible to the user.

[BUG] The recurring-event cancellation path iterates credentials with forEach(async ...) that is never awaited, so the callback's awaits (getCalendar, and any delete/update calls pushed to integrationsToDelete) run concurrently with the code that follows. The handler proceeds to consume integrationsToDelete before the forEach callbacks have finished, so cancel operations for the later calendar credentials either arrive too late to be awaited (their rejections become unhandled) or are missed entirely from the deletion batch, while the cancellation API responds success.

[ADVISORY] The pre-refactor legacy deletion path was converted from a fire-and-forget push to a sequential for...of with an awaited getCalendar per credential, serializing what were previously parallel-started operations. Users cancelling legacy bookings with many calendar credentials now wait for each dynamic import plus calendar deletion sequentially before the cancel response; a slow first calendar (e.g. hung Exchange) delays or times out the whole cancel request. Counter-argument: awaiting is the correctness fix for the async getCalendar; but the loop could be Promise.all without losing that correctness.

[ADVISORY] Every app's dynamic import() promise is created eagerly at module-load time and awaited ad-hoc at each consumer site with no rejection handling. Any single package that throws at module scope (bad env, missing optional dependency) produces an unhandled promise rejection at process startup or at each first await with no contextual log, and since all 30 imports start immediately the code-splitting benefit is limited to async deferral only. Counter-argument: static imports had the same eager-load failure mode; but the failure shape changed from a synchronous, stack-attributed module load error to a floating rejected promise.

goldens.comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces multiple `forEach(async (...) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` patterns (e.g., `packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts`, `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts`, `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx`). `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await async callbacks, so the returned promises from `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` are discarded and the surrounding flow can proceed before deletions complete. Additionally, because `getCalendar` now awaits a dynamic import via `await appStore[...]`, any rejection inside these async callbacks can become an unhandled promise rejection since nothing awaits/catches the callback promises.

adjudication.rationale: In multiple places the diff changes `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => { ... })` to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` (e.g. `packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts`, `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts`, `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx`). `forEach` does not await async callbacks, so the `await getCalendar(...)` and the subsequent `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` run asynchronously without being awaited/collected. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The entire appStore is converted from resolved modules to pending dynamic-import Promises in a sweeping cross-package refactor, yet the diff contains no test files (no *.test.*, *.spec.*, spec/, test/ paths) verifying any of the awaited call-site conversions. A single missed await at any appStore consumer outside the diff compiles away nothing at runtime — the site silently receives a Promise (truthy, fails the `"lib" in app` check with a TypeError on a Promise lacking `lib`) and the integration is reported 'not implemented' with no test to catch the regression; the async-conversion behaviors (getVideoAdapters rewrite, deleteEvent async, getConnectedCalendars await) are all unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff converts `packages/app-store/index.ts` entries from eagerly imported modules to `import(...)` Promises (e.g., `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")`), forcing many call sites to add `await` (e.g., `await appStore[...]` in `getCalendar`, `videoClient`, payment handlers). No test/spec files are added in this PR to validate that these awaited conversions work end-to-end and to catch any remaining consumers that might still read from `appStore` without awaiting. While the finding speculates about consumers “outside the diff” (not verifiable here) and overstates a TypeError for the `'lib' in app` check (a Promise is an object so it typically just evaluates false), the core diff-grounded concern—major runtime behavior change with no accompanying tests—is valid and specific to this refactor.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The getVideoAdapters rewrite from reduce to for-loop is behavior-bearing new logic (it fixes the old early-`return acc` that skipped subsequent credentials) with no test in the diff. adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the old `reduce` implementation: returning `acc` inside the callback does not short-circuit `reduce`, so it did not “skip subsequent credentials.” Both old and new code iterate all credentials and only add adapters when `app && "lib" in app && "VideoApiAdapter" in app.lib` holds. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The module still eagerly loads every app package at evaluation time, so the PR's stated intent of deferring package loading is not actually achieved. Anyone expecting startup/import-time savings or true lazy loading gets none: `import("./applecalendar")` etc. are invoked immediately when app-store/index.ts is evaluated, kicking off all chunk fetches at once — only the await points became async, not the loading. In a server bundle this is roughly equivalent to the old static imports; the diff converts the whole codebase to async call sites without delivering the corresponding benefit.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/index.ts`, `appStore` now stores `import("./...")` expressions directly (e.g. `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")`). Those dynamic imports are executed when the module is evaluated, creating Promises for *all* apps immediately, rather than deferring import until a specific key is accessed. The diff then updates call sites to `await appStore[...]`, but this doesn’t by itself provide true lazy/on-demand loading; it just makes consumers async while still kicking off all imports up front.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Converting the recurring-event cancellation loop's forEach callback to async defers the apiDeletes pushes until after the surrounding code has already collected and awaited them, so recurring-event deletions are dropped from the awaited batch. For a recurring booking cancellation, the loop awaits getCalendar before pushing the delete/update promises; any caller that does Promise.all(apiDeletes) immediately after the forEach resolves without those deletions, and failures inside the async callbacks surface as unhandled rejections. Previously getCalendar was synchronous so the pushes happened before collection — this diff introduces the race.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `getCalendar` async and then changes several loops to `forEach(async ...)` with `await getCalendar(...)` inside (e.g. `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts` around the recurring booking branch, `packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts`, `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts`, and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx`). Because `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await async callbacks, any side effects after the first `await` (e.g., pushing promises into a batch array or executing deletes/updates) can occur after the surrounding code continues, so awaited batches can miss operations and errors can become unhandled rejections. This race did not exist when `getCalendar` was synchronous.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The dynamic import() calls are invoked eagerly at module-evaluation time inside the appStore object literal, so every app package still loads at startup — the diff adds async ceremony without achieving lazy loading. The stated goal (async import of appStore packages, reduced startup bundle/work) is not achieved: all 28 packages are still imported at process start, now additionally as 28 floating promises; whoever later 'optimizes' by assuming modules load on first use will be wrong, and startup gets no benefit from this refactor while every call site pays an await.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/index.ts`, the refactor replaces static imports with an object literal whose values are `import("./...")` expressions (e.g. `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")`). Those `import()` calls are executed when the module is evaluated, meaning all listed modules begin loading at startup anyway (now as stored Promises), rather than being deferred until first use. This is a real, diff-grounded performance/architecture issue (async overhead without true lazy loading), but it does not by itself constitute a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 28 unhandled import() promises created at module load have no .catch, so a single failed dynamic import (e.g. a broken optional peer dependency in one app package) becomes a process-wide unhandledRejection. In any deployment where one app package fails to load (native dep missing, syntax error introduced), the whole server process dies on unhandledRejection (or logs it at boot) even for tenants that never use that app — a single app's failure cascades to all tenants, the exact failure mode the appStore isolation was meant to prevent.
matched_golden_ids: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments point to the same underlying problem: dynamic import/await failures are not being handled, leading to unhandled promise rejections. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The dynamic import() calls are evaluated eagerly at module-init of packages/app-store, so every one of the 28 app packages starts loading the moment any file imports appStore — the PR's stated objective of deferring appStore package loading is not achieved. Any serverless function or client bundle importing appStore transitively still kicks off all 28 package fetches at import time; cold-start and bundle-size savings the change was accepted for never materialize, while the whole codebase pays the async access cost — an objective change nobody accepted the tradeoff for. To get real laziness the store needs `() => import(...)` thunks or top-level await decisions per app.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/index.ts`, the store now assigns each key to the result of calling `import("./...")` (e.g. `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")`). Achieving true per-app laziness would require storing thunks like `() => import(...)` (or similar), not already-invoked imports. This is a diff-grounded performance/architecture issue, not a functional correctness defect shown by the diff.

For recurring-booking cancellation, calendar event deletions race the request lifecycle; a failed await getCalendar/deleteEvent is swallowed as an unhandled rejection and the user's calendar keeps events for a booking that Cal.com reports as cancelled — silent data divergence between the app and the external calendar.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows multiple instances changed to `forEach(async ...)` with `await getCalendar(...)` inside, but the returned Promises are not awaited/collected. In the recurring cancellation branch of `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts` the code does `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... })` without awaiting the loop, so calendar deletions/updates can race request completion and failures can surface as unhandled rejections. Similar patterns were introduced in `packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts`, `wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts`, and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getCalendarCredentials now stores an unawaited Promise<Calendar|null> in each item's calendar field while only one consumer (getConnectedCalendars line ~47) was updated to `await item.calendar`. Any other current or near-future consumer of getCalendarCredentials that reads item.calendar directly gets a Promise instead of a Calendar, and `'calendar' in item` style checks pass while `calendar.deleteEvent` would throw TypeError on the Promise; the next change to this file gets riskier because the invariant (sync value vs Promise) depends on the consumer's discipline.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `getCalendar` becomes `async` and `getCalendarCredentials` still assigns `const calendar = getCalendar(credential);` without awaiting, so each returned item’s `calendar` property will indeed be a `Promise<Calendar | null>`. Only `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to `const calendar = await item.calendar;`. While the diff doesn’t show another concrete consumer currently breaking at runtime, the exported helper now returns a mixed/implicit contract (calendar vs promise) that can easily be misused elsewhere (e.g., calling `item.calendar.deleteEvent` would fail), making future changes riskier.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] forEach(async ...) discards the returned deleteEvent/deleteMeeting promises, so rejections are unhandled and the enclosing try/catch cannot catch them. During reschedule, a failing calendar deleteEvent rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection while the reschedule itself completes and reports success, leaving the stale calendar event on the remote provider with no log, no error result, and no rollback.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); ... })` in multiple places (e.g., `packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts`, `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts`, `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx`). `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await async callbacks, so the returned `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` promises are not awaited/collected; any rejection will occur after the surrounding synchronous `try/catch` has exited and can become an unhandled rejection. This can let reschedule flows complete without surfacing provider deletion failures, matching the finding.

During reschedule, a failing calendar deleteEvent rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection while the reschedule completes and reports success, orphaning the old event on the remote calendar with no surfaced error.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces multiple `forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` patterns (e.g. `packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts`, `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts`, `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx`). `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await or aggregate returned promises, so any rejection from `await getCalendar(...)` or from `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`/`deleteMeeting(...)` will not be caught by the surrounding synchronous `try/catch`, and will surface as an unhandled promise rejection while the outer reschedule flow continues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] forEach(async ...) discards the returned deleteEvent promises, so rejections are unhandled by any surrounding error handling. A reschedule whose calendar deleteEvent rejects still returns a successful tRPC response; the old event stays on the user's calendar and the rejection surfaces only as an unhandled promise rejection, invisible to the user.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` in multiple places (e.g., `packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts`, `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts`, and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx`). `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await or collect the returned promises, so any rejection from `deleteEvent` (or other awaited calls inside the callback) will not be caught by surrounding synchronous `try/catch` and will not be awaited before returning from the parent function/handler. This matches the finding: failures can be silently ignored and surface as unhandled promise rejections, while the reschedule flow can proceed as if successful.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The recurring-event cancellation path iterates credentials with forEach(async ...) that is never awaited, so the callback's awaits (getCalendar, and any delete/update calls pushed to integrationsToDelete) run concurrently with the code that follows. The handler proceeds to consume integrationsToDelete before the forEach callbacks have finished, so cancel operations for the later calendar credentials either arrive too late to be awaited (their rejections become unhandled) or are missed entirely from the deletion batch, while the cancellation API responds success.

adjudication.rationale: In the recurring-event branch of `handleCancelBooking.ts`, the diff shows `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... integrationsToDelete.push(...) })`. An `async` callback passed to `forEach` is not awaited by `forEach`, so any awaited work inside (notably the new `await getCalendar(...)` after `getCalendar` became async) can complete after the surrounding handler continues. This can cause `integrationsToDelete` to be consumed (e.g., via `Promise.all(...)` later in the handler) before all promises have been pushed, and any later rejections may become unhandled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The pre-refactor legacy deletion path was converted from a fire-and-forget push to a sequential for...of with an awaited getCalendar per credential, serializing what were previously parallel-started operations. Users cancelling legacy bookings with many calendar credentials now wait for each dynamic import plus calendar deletion sequentially before the cancel response; a slow first calendar (e.g. hung Exchange) delays or times out the whole cancel request. Counter-argument: awaiting is the correctness fix for the async getCalendar; but the loop could be Promise.all without losing that correctness.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleCancelBooking.ts` the legacy path changed from starting deletions immediately for each credential (`.forEach((credential) => { const calendar = getCalendar(credential); apiDeletes.push(calendar?.deleteEvent(...)) })`) to a `for...of` loop that does `const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); apiDeletes.push(calendar?.deleteEvent(...))`. Since `getCalendar` is now `async` (due to dynamic `import()` in `app-store/index.ts` and `await appStore[...]` in `getCalendar.ts`), this loop serializes each dynamic import (and any calendar construction inside `getCalendar`) before the next deletion is even enqueued. The finding’s suggestion that `Promise.all(calendarCredentials.map(async ...))` could restore parallelism while remaining correct is diff-grounded. This is a performance/latency regression risk rather than a verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Every app's dynamic import() promise is created eagerly at module-load time and awaited ad-hoc at each consumer site with no rejection handling. Any single package that throws at module scope (bad env, missing optional dependency) produces an unhandled promise rejection at process startup or at each first await with no contextual log, and since all 30 imports start immediately the code-splitting benefit is limited to async deferral only. Counter-argument: static imports had the same eager-load failure mode; but the failure shape changed from a synchronous, stack-attributed module load error to a floating rejected promise.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `packages/app-store/index.ts` from static imports to an object whose values are `import("./...")` promises created immediately at module initialization (e.g. `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")`). Call sites now do ad-hoc `await appStore[...]` (e.g. `getCalendar` and `getVideoAdapters`) without any local rejection handling, so any failing dynamic import would propagate as a rejected promise with limited contextual logging, and the eager creation means all ~30 imports start right away (reducing the intended lazy-loading/code-splitting benefit). This is a concrete design/robustness issue introduced by the change, even though it only manifests if an import fails.
